sync.no_files_desc: Files appear here once the first sync has run.
sync.overwrite_warning: Days that were corrected by hand are normally left alone. This run will replace them with whatever the file says. That cannot be undone.

work_schedules.page_hint: Describes the working week. Nothing here changes a recorded attendance day — it is the reference the attendance checks will be built on.
work_schedules.no_schedules_desc: Create one to describe the working week for this company.
work_schedules.case_summary: Case opens past {{late}} min late / {{early}} min early
work_schedules.unassigned_warning: {{count}} employee(s) have no schedule assigned. They fall back to the company default, or to nothing if there is none.
work_schedules.no_holidays_desc: Without a holiday calendar, every public holiday would later be counted as an absence.
work_schedules.break_hint: The break is deducted by policy. The attendance feed reports only the first and last punch of the day, so time away at lunch can never be measured.
work_schedules.threshold_hint: Within grace, nothing is recorded. Past grace the minutes are recorded, but a reviewable case only opens past the case thresholds.
work_schedules.effective_hint: Earlier days keep the schedule that was in force at the time — this does not change history.

attendance_eval.title: Attendance Checks
attendance_eval.subtitle: What the schedule engine makes of each day, compared against what is recorded.
attendance_eval.shadow_banner_title: Shadow mode — nothing here has been applied
attendance_eval.shadow_banner_body: The engine judges each day against the employee’s work schedule and records its opinion separately. No attendance record, status or payroll figure has been changed by any of it. This is here so the two can be compared before the engine is trusted with the real columns.
attendance_eval.no_cases_desc: The engine found no problems in this period — or it has not been run yet.
attendance_eval.offboarding_no_end_date: {{status}} with no end date — the absences are probably that, not real ones
attendance_eval.no_diffs: The engine agrees with every record
attendance_eval.no_diffs_desc: No day in this period is judged differently from what is stored.
attendance_eval.no_runs: The checks have not been run yet
attendance_eval.no_runs_desc: Run them for a date range to see what the engine makes of it.
attendance_eval.run_line: {{days}} day(s) evaluated · {{rows}} row(s) annotated · {{opened}} case(s) opened · {{closed}} closed · {{differs}} disagreement(s)
attendance_eval.days_not_observed: No attendance file covered: {{days}} — no absences were raised for those days.
attendance_eval.dormant: No punches at all in this range, so no absences were raised: {{names}}
attendance_eval.untracked: Not registered on the fingerprint device: {{names}}
attendance_eval.shadow_complete: Observation period complete — ready to review
attendance_eval.waive_hint: Waive — no reason needed, no cost
attendance_eval.days_hint: Pre-filled from the time actually lost ({{suggested}}). Change it if policy says otherwise.
attendance_eval.note_placeholder: What the employee said, or the decision taken
attendance_eval.effect_paid: {{name}} is paid. The time is excused and nothing is deducted.
attendance_eval.effect_unpaid: {{name}} is unpaid. {{days}} of a day will be deducted on the next payroll run.
attendance_eval.no_report_desc: Once the checks have run, each employee's absences and lateness appear here.
attendance_eval.report_note: Paid and unpaid days come from the reasons recorded against each case. Unpaid days are what payroll will deduct.
